The five-day exclusive window for negotiating with pending free agents expired along with the deadline for setting each team’s 40-man roster on today. Then the real fun begins with all free agents open to negotiate with any team they choose and deciding if they want to sign before the CBA expires or take their chances with the status of the game after the new contract is signed. Fritz was the bullpen coach under Larry Rothschild until Rothschild’s firing in 2021. He assumed the primary job for the remainder of that season and then became the bullpen coach again when Ruben Niebla was hired prior to the 2022 season. Bullpen losses The news on Oct. 30 was the first blow to the Padres bullpen. Bullpen coach Ben Fritz , a member of the Padres coaching staff since 2015, was hired away by the Arizona Diamondbacks to be their pitching coach. Fritz was the bullpen coach under Larry Rothschild until Rothschild’s firing in 2021. He assumed the primary job for the remainder of that season and then became the bullpen coach again when Ruben Niebla was hired prior to the 2022 season. As the shepherd of one of the best bullpens in baseball over the past several seasons, the Padres gave Fritz a big raise last offseason to keep him on staff. He had reportedly been targeted by several other teams as their pitching coach. LHP Adrián Morejón is a free agent. The Padres’ closer, Mason Miller, acknowledged Morejón’s value to the bullpen, saying he believed he was the most valuable reliever in MLB. In an article by Dennis Lin in The Athletic on Sept. 14, Miller stated, “He’s the most valuable reliever on our team and, I would argue, in baseball too.” It remains to be seen if the Padres can offer the reliever a contract that will keep him in San Diego. His projected value, which ranges from 3 years and $42 million by Jim Bowden ( The Athletic ) to 5 years and $90 million by Joel Reuter (Bleacher Report), might not be in the budget for the Friars due to the lack of starting arms on the roster. Morejón has stated on multiple occasions his desire to stay with the Padres but team-friendly free agent deals are mostly nonexistent in modern baseball. If the team can come up with a creative deal to keep Morejón, A.J. Preller will need to keep the top priority on the starting rotation. Keeping Hart, Matsui, Peralta and Estrada The Padres got very lucky when LHP Yuki Matsui opted to remain with the team. He had a player option to make himself a free agent but decided to accept his $6.5 million salary for 2027 and has another option in 2028. After signing with the Padres before the 2024 season, Matsui posted a 3.86 ERA over the first two seasons with the team. Coming to MLB after dominating as a closer in Japan, Matsui was unable to replicate that success. He pitched well but wasn’t able to repeat his dominance. Making some adjustments to his pitch arsenal before the 2026 season, Matsui went back to featuring his slider and improved his effectiveness. In 64 innings of relief, Matsui lowered his ERA to 1.83 without a significant change in walk or strikeout rates. By staying in the fold, Matsui saves the Padres the need to find a high-leverage replacement for the 31-year-old lefty. LHP Kyle Hart had an up-and-down 2026. He had stretches of valuable effectiveness and a few blow-up appearances. He finished the season with a 4.92 ERA in 64 innings pitched. The Padres exercised his $2.5 million team option, keeping the 34-year-old in the bullpen for the 2027 season. This most likely represents the team’s need to keep the bullpen as intact as possible for the next season. His salary is reasonable for a pitcher who can pitch at any point in a game and for more than one inning. LHP Wandy Peralta opted in for the third and final time in his four-year contract with the Padres. He signed a 4-year, $16.5 million deal before the 2024 season and has a sub-4 ERA with the Padres for his time in the bullpen. In 2026, he finished with a 3.61 ERA in 77.1 innings. Peralta was left off the postseason roster after losing effectiveness at the end of the season. RHP Jeremiah Estrada is arbitration-eligible for the first time this offseason. He will need to be offered a contract by Nov. 20 for his first opportunity at arbitration. His 2026 season was injury-marred, and that will probably affect the offer he gets for his first contract year. Only throwing 31 innings for the year, Estrada finished with a 3.48 ERA. He had both shoulder and leg injuries that limited his availability and effectiveness. Arbitration-eligible Closer Mason Miller is in his second year of arbitration eligibility and stands to earn a big raise from his $4 million 2026 salary. After posting 38 saves and a 1.67 ERA in 70 innings pitched, Miller is projected to earn $8.1 million, according to MLB TradeRumors. RHP Bryan Hoeing, who again spent most of the season on the injured list with flexor tendon surgery, is projected to be offered $0.8 million in arbitration. He should be healthy to start 2027. RHP Jhony Brito is arbitration-eligible and is projected to be offered $0.8 million for 2027. He spent part of 2026 on the injured list from his Tommy John surgery and then completed his rehab in time to log innings in El Paso and pitch nine innings for the Padres. He should be a contender for the either the bullpen or possibly as a starter in 2027. The rest of the bullpen RHP David Morgan , RHP Bradgley Rodriguez , RHP Hunter Stratton , and RHP Garret Hawkins are under contract and on the 40-man roster for the 2027 season. All should be in the running for bullpen spots when the 2027 spring camp begins. Other options The status of Joe Musgrove is undetermined but it would be a big surprise if he isn’t in the mix for the starting rotation in 2027. Pitching three innings from the bullpen in the 2026 postseason showed that Musgrove can still pitch. The questions are about his ability to bounce back from his outings. His health will most likely be determined during the spring of 2027. These 11 players will be joined by the pitchers signed by the organization during free agency or acquired by trade. There are also several minor league pitchers who could be added to the roster before being left available for the Rule 5 draft. As it stands, the bullpen only lacks Morejón from the dominant bullpen seen in 2026. It should remain a strength for the 2027 Padres.

item.title: UTSA opens season with lopsided loss at San Jose State
item.description: UTSA guard Isaiah Coleman, left, keeps the ball from guard Shey Eberwein during practice at the school's new Basketball & Volleyball Training Center in San Antonio, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) San Jose State dominated on the interior to send UTSA to a season-opening loss, as the Spartans toppled the Roadrunners 95-74 on Monday at Provident Credit Union Event Center in San Jose, Calif. San Jose State closed the opening half with a 17-2 run across just more than five minutes, taking an 18-point lead into the break. The Spartans kept the cushion at double digits the rest of the way, leading by as many as 27 points. Joey Chammaa scored 27 and Mekhi Mason added 26 as San Jose State scored 46 points in the paint, shot 23 of 30 (76.7%) on two-point shots and built a 43-22 advantage in rebounding. READ MORE: With Claunch suspended following DWI arrest, UTSA faces new questions Preston Turner and Shey Eberwein each scored 15 points to lead UTSA, while Isaiah Coleman had 12 and KJ Tenner notched 11 with a team-high six assists. The Roadrunners also forced 21 turnovers. UTSA was led by acting coach Nick Bowman, who stepped into the role when coach Austin Claunch was suspended Wednesday following his arrest on suspicion of DWI. The Roadrunners will play their home opener against VMI at 4 p.m. Saturday. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Michigan basketball overpowers Oakland in Mike Boynton Jr. U-M debut
item.description: Michigan basketball opened the 2026-27 season the way it closed the previous one: with a victory. The stakes certainly weren't as high as April's NCAA Tournament win over UConn, but MIke Boynton Jr.'s debut as Michigan coach was still a success, with the Wolverines eventually finding their rhythm with separate 13-4 and 9-0 spurts in the second half, fueling a 84-68 win over Greg Kampe's Oakland Golden Grizzlies at Crisler Center on Monday, Nov. 2. Michigan, which is planning a 3-point-heavy offense this season, was cold all night beyond the arc, going just 6-for-33 (18.2%). But the Wolverines controlled the transition game (outscoring OU, 19-0, on fastbreak points) and made the most of their second chances, rebounding 41% of their misses for 23 second-chance points. DREAMING OF DETROIT: 4 reasons Michigan basketball can return to 2027 Final Four in Detroit Michigan came sloppy, with four turnovers and a 7-2 OU run in the opening five minutes of the second half. Finally, true freshman Quinn Costello hit a deep 3 from the right wing that helped turn things around, and he scored eight of U-M's next 10 points to build a 14-point lead. While Oakland hit shots early, U-M's defense was solid. Michigan forced the Golden Grizzlies to play one-on-one instead of generating offense through movement; OU had just five assists on 20 made shots. It's a big reason Oakland had a 9:31 stretch in the second in which it went 1-of-15 from the floor, which gave U-M room to separate, even with Oakland in the double bonus for the final 10 minutes of the game. Oakland got as close as seven behind a 7-0 run with 8:34 to play, but U-M responded with a 9-0 spurt of its own, highlighted by an Oscar Goodman Euro-step layup in transition to pull away for good. item.title: Shohei Ohtani Extends Remarkable MVP Streak Despite Injury-Plagued Season
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani was an MVP finalist once again, marking yet another milestone of greatness for the Japanese import. Ohtani gets another MVP nomination Ohtani was officially named one of three Baseball Writers’ Association of America finalists for the National League MVP award. This marks his sixth straight season as an MVP finalist, and his third straight with the Dodgers. Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after hitting a three-run home run during the second inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Why Ohtani won’t win the MVP Ohtani is expected to finish second or third in the MVP voting , given that he missed time on the injured list and his hitting production dipped as he battled injuries. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) All things considered, it was a great year, with a .275/.377/.512/.889 slash line, a 1.79 ERA, and 95 strikeouts in 14 starts. However, he stopped pitching after early July, and along with his hitting slump, he totaled just 30 home runs. Still, Ohtani posted 6.6 fWAR and 6.5 bWAR, with the potential to be much higher. Oct 11, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Shohei Ohtani (17) looks on before game one of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs against the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Pete Crow-Armstrong, meanwhile, delivered a historic season of his own, with a 9.8 bWAR and 10.6 fWAR. He did it on both ends, hitting 45 home runs and stealing 41 bases while posting the best center field defense in the big leagues. Ohtani has no chance of surpassing Crow-Armstrong, even at his peak, because Crow-Armstrong has the national narrative and the production to put him in a great spot to win Ohtani’s long-held award. Dave Roberts, back in August, acknowledged PCA’s greatness this year. “I’ve followed what Pete’s doing and he’s figured some things out with the bat,” Roberts said. “He’s having a heck of a year. He has rightfully made it a lot closer than most people would expect. He’s having a tremendous season… he’s done a lot of things with the bat that has made him viable versus left. Which has made him more of a complete player. “He’s having an MVP-type season.” Now, an MVP-type season is on the verge of becoming an MVP-winning season, all of which will motivate Ohtani for 2027.

item.title: Cubs reward reliever with new contract after spectacular 2026 season
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Cubs reward reliever with new contract after spectacular 2026 season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Cubs have agreed to a new one-year contract with veteran right-handed reliever Jacob Webb, the team announced on Monday. Webb will reportedly receive a $2 million salary for the 2027 season, with a $4 million club option for 2028 that includes a $500,000 buyout. The deal guarantees him $2.5 million, while performance incentives could add another $500,000 to his earnings. Moreover, he will receive an additional $125,000 upon reaching 35, 45, 55 and 65 appearances. The new agreement replaces Webb’s previous contract , which included a $2.5 million team option for 2027 without a buyout. Rather than simply exercising that option, Chicago restructured the arrangement to secure another potential season of control over the 33-year-old. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The decision comes after Webb’s superlative campaign accomplished against the backdrop of considerable upheaval in the Cubs’ pitching ranks. He appeared in 68 games, finishing with a 3.36 ERA across 67 innings while collecting a career-best 73 strikeouts against 25 walks. He also recorded nine saves and nine holds, leading the team in saves. Webb assumed heightened importance when injuries and inconsistent performances created uncertainty in the bullpen. Manager Craig Counsell eventually entrusted him with closing responsibilities, and he responded with an outstanding stretch during the summer. Between June and August, Webb completed 24 consecutive appearances without surrendering a run, covering 24 1/3 innings. That performance tied for the third-longest single-season scoreless appearance streak in franchise history. Only Andrew Chafin, with 26 games in 2021, and Warren Brusstar, with 25 in 1983, recorded longer streaks. His underlying numbers were equally encouraging. Webb produced a 25.7% strikeout rate and a 33.3% whiff rate, placing him in the 96th percentile across MLB in the latter category. His mid-90s four-seam fastball and mid-80s changeup were particularly effective, with the changeup generating a 41.5% whiff rate. However, Webb did struggle toward the end of the season, compiling a 9.90 ERA across his final 11 appearances. He still managed 1 1/3 scoreless innings in Chicago’s Game 1 loss to the San Diego Padres in the National League Wild Card Series. With several Cubs pitchers heading toward free agency, retaining Webb gives the team a dependable bullpen option for 2027. His return also heralds the organization’s opening gambit in rebuilding a pitching staff expected to undergo considerable changes this offseason . item.title: Cubs extend Seiya Suzuki $23.15 million qualifying offer
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Cubs extend Seiya Suzuki $23.15 million qualifying offer appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Cubs extended a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer to outfielder Seiya Suzuki on Monday, giving the veteran a chance to return for the 2027 season while protecting their ability to receive draft compensation if he leaves. Suzuki’s 2026 production included 26 home runs, 86 RBI and 96 runs across 143 games for the Cubs. The 32-year-old posted a .270/.368/.473 slash line and an .841 OPS. The productive season closed out the five-year, $85 million contract Suzuki signed with the Cubs, putting his future in focus as the offseason begins. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) USA Today’s Bob Nightengale included Suzuki among eight qualifying-offer recipients in his Monday report , the second-fewest in a full season since the system began in 2012. “Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki: Final year of 5-year, $85 million contract.” Suzuki has until November 17 to accept or decline the offer. Accepting would keep him with the Cubs for another season at the designated salary. Declining would allow him to continue pursuing a longer agreement, either with Chicago or another club. If Suzuki rejects the offer and signs elsewhere, the Cubs would receive a compensatory draft pick. Because Chicago exceeded the competitive balance tax threshold, that selection would come after the fourth round. The offer does not settle Suzuki’s future in Chicago. He and the Cubs can still negotiate a separate deal. Chicago declined to extend qualifying offers to fellow free agents Ian Happ and Matthew Boyd, leaving Suzuki as the club’s sole recipient this offseason. The Cubs’ next move hinges on Suzuki’s decision , which will determine whether they retain the productive outfielder on a one-year contract or continue through free agency with draft-pick compensation at stake. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Combine that with Michigan somehow losing the rebounding battle to a small Oakland team (44-42) and there’s plenty of room for improvement heading into the UConn game. item.title: Dodge announces return to NASCAR Cup Series in 2027
item.description: Motorsport photo Dodge is returning to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, becoming the fourth manufacturer on the grid alongside Chevrolet, Toyota, and Ford. This is a year earlier than most projections, and there will be a tight turn-around for next season. This was officially announced at the SEMA Show in Las Vegas on Monday evening. The manufacturer will partner with Kaulig Racing , which currently runs Chevrolets at the Cup level. However, the team also fields a fleet of five Ram 1500s in the Truck Series, which Stellantis brought back to the third level of NASCAR ahead of the 2026 season. The Dodge entries will utilize engines built by ECR, which provides Chevrolet engines to teams like Richard Childress Racing , Trackhouse Racing, and Kaulig Racing. Kaulig is expected to retain their current driver lineup of A.J. Allmendinger in the No. 16 and Ty Dillon in the No. 10. The team has two wins in the Cup Series, both with Allmendinger, at the Indianapolis Road Course in 2021 and the Charlotte Roval in 2023. Dodge has a lengthy history in NASCAR, dating all the way back to 1950. They won two manufacturer titles in 1970 and 1975, but they also won several driver’s championships. NASCAR legend Richard Petty drove a Dodge to three of his seven Cup Series titles in the ‘70s, and Brad Keselowski won the 2012 Cup title in a Dodge in what ultimately became their last year of competition until this latest revival. They disappeared from the grid when the Gen-6 car was introduced in 2013, and there have only been three manufacturers at the Cup level ever since. The Next Gen car may make the transition easier, as they don't have to build the entire car from the ground up like previous eras and instead will utilize NASCAR's extensive network of external suppliers. To make matters worse, Estrella picked up his third foul at the 18:11 mark and McKenney followed suit four minutes later. Despite all that, Michigan kept Oakland at bay. item.description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Lightweight-turned Welterweight Ignacio Bahamondes may not be the only member of his family headed for big things. His younger brother, Alberth Bahamondes , scored a violent first-round knockout over Contender Series veteran Joey Hart in the “Featured Bout” of LFA 245 this past weekend (Fri., Oct. 30, 2026) inside Seneca Niagara Event Center in Niagara Falls, New York. After spending the opening minute feinting and studying Hart’s reactions, Bahamondes suddenly exploded forward with a crisp one-two combination. Hart immediately found himself retreating as “La Jaulita” swarmed him with another barrage of punches. The pressure proved too much. Bahamondes dropped Hart to the canvas and followed him down with several unanswered ground-and-pound shots, forcing the referee to intervene. Watch the finish below: Alberth Bahamondes def. Joey Hart via KO in Round 1 at 1:00 📲 @VICETV @FloSports @ESPNKnockout @ESPNDeportes 🇺🇸 #LFANewYork #LFA245 pic.twitter.com/WxYZKaPYyM — LFA (@LFAfighting) October 31, 2026 View this post on Instagram Not a bad way to introduce yourself to LFA. Bahamondes improved his professional record to 8-1 at just 18 years old, with older brother Ignacio in his corner to watch the latest addition to the family highlight reel. The Chilean prospect has now won three consecutive fights since suffering the lone defeat of his career via split decision. All eight of his professional victories have come by stoppage, including seven in the first round. LFA has long served as one of UFC’s most reliable developmental pipelines, and Bahamondes will probably eventually follow his brother into the Octagon if he continues producing performances like this. At only 18, however, there is no reason to rush his development. As for Hart (9-5), the loss snapped his two-fight winning streak. A year ago, Jódar was in a similar spot. He won three Challenger titles in 2025, including the Charlottesville Challenger in November, climbed to a career-high No. 166 and qualified for the Next Gen ATP Finals. For a while, it looked like he might return for the spring. Instead, on Dec. 31, he announced he was forgoing his remaining eligibility to turn pro. Ten months later, he has reached the Roland Garros quarterfinals and a Masters 1000 final in Shanghai, and he is the first man to reach the top 10 in his first ATP Tour season. Dietrich is now ranked close to where Jódar was when he left. He has made it clear his story will end differently. Until last fall, pro tennis was not even the plan. “The plan was to do an internship in New York, and then work in New York after school,” Dietrich told Cracked Racquets’ Alex Gruskin after beating Brooksby. From there: Second round: beat Georgia’s Noah Johnston 6-3, 6-3 Quarterfinals: beat Tanishk Konduri 6-7 (4), 6-4, 6-0 Semifinals: beat 6-seed Jack Anthrop 3-6, 7-6 (4), 6-3 Final: beat Jerry Roddick 3-6, 6-2, 6-1 Four of his five matches went three sets, and he had to work from behind after losing the first set in all four of them. The title caps a fall that has already secured his place at the NCAA Individual Championships. At the ITA Atlantic Regional in Blacksburg on Oct. 12, Santamarta Roig beat teammate Stiles Brockett 6-2, 3-6, 6-1 in the singles semifinals to qualify for NCAA singles. That same day, he and third-year Jangjun Kim won the regional doubles title over Virginia Tech’s Blake Hilsen and Eyal Shumilov, 6-7 (3), 6-4, 10-8, which put them in the NCAA doubles draw too. It is a big step from May. In the national final, Santamarta Roig played No. 4 singles against Texas and lost to Oliver Ojakaar 6-1, 6-4. Coming into this season, Santamarta Roig has demonstrated an improved serve and backhand, which has led to his sophomore leap. What is next This week: the Charlottesville Challenger (Nov. 1-8) at the Boar’s Head Sports Club. Both title winners are back home, and Virginia already has a win on the board: Jack Kennedy , the No. 1 recruit in the class of 2026, beat No. 275 Hynek Barton 7-5, 1-6, 6-3 on Monday to reach the round of 16. Dietrich opens Tuesday against top seed Marcos Giron, ranked No. 88. Santamarta Roig received a wild card and plays 5-seed Clement Chidekh (No. 134) on Tuesday. Dietrich and Mans Dahlberg , last fall’s NCAA doubles champions, reunite in doubles against 4-seeds Jarno Jans and Joran Vliegen. Stiles Brockett beat 12-seed Emile Hudd (No. 461) 6-3, 5-7, 6-4 in the first round of qualifying on Sunday, then lost to 6-seed Andres Martin 6-3, 6-0 in the second round on Monday. Jangjun Kim lost in qualifying to No. 407 Ozan Baris, 6-3, 6-4. NCAA Individual Championships (Nov. 17-22, Athens, Ga.). Santamarta Roig is in the singles and doubles draws, along with Keegan Rice and Luca Preda in singles and Kim in doubles. Remaining Cavaliers get one more chance to qualify at the ITA Sectionals in Charlottesville, Nov. 5-8. Dietrich, who has not played an ITA event this fall, will not be in Athens, according to Division1Tennis. That says less about Virginia than about where his game is right now. Dietrich knows how rare this stretch is. “I’m trying to make the best out of this last year, learn as much as possible and have a good time with the guys as well,” he told Gruskin. “It is truly a special time.”

item.description: Credit to Arsenal for restricting opportunities at Anfield but Iraola will need his side to learn to unpick low backlines Liverpool did not have a shot on target in their 1-0 defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, according to Opta, the first time they have drawn this type of blank in a Premier League game at Anfield since records began in 2003-04. They did not find the target in a goalless draw at the Emirates Stadium this year either, though in both games they struck the woodwork. The margins tend to be fine when recording statistical outliers. If Alexis Mac Allister’s floated ball from distance into David Raya’s waiting arms had actually counted as a shot, would Andoni Iraola’s side have delivered a markedly better attacking performance? Far more concerning for the Spaniard will be that his team had 52 touches in the Arsenal penalty area (which is good) to create only one Opta‑defined big chance (which is bad). The Premier League average this season is five times more efficient; 10.3 box touches per big chance. Continue reading...

item.title: Arsenal have everything they need to repeat as Premier League champions | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Sunday’s win at Liverpool showed the Gunners are deeper, more experienced, and are playing against a weaker class of contenders than last season Sign up for our free newsletter here Arsenal are three points clear at the top of the Premier League table . The season of domination that many anticipated from the champions appears to be coming to pass. Liverpool challenged them on Sunday. There was a 20-minute spell before half-time when they swarmed all over Arsenal, and Anfield felt at least like it did in the golden years of Jürgen Klopp, when it buzzed with an energy that could overwhelm visitors. But Arsenal got through that, reset at half-time, and navigated the second half with relative comfort. For the second league game running, they denied Liverpool a shot on target. item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
